seoTitle: Integrate Shiprocket Checkout with Shopify (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Connect Shiprocket to your Shopify store: start the channel from Shiprocket's dashboard, authorize with your login, set pickup and rates for India, and confirm orders sync automatically.
intro:
Shiprocket is the shipping layer most Indian Shopify stores end up on, because it aggregates courier partners, handles COD, and pushes tracking back to the customer without you negotiating with each carrier yourself. The integration itself is short: install the app, authorize it with your Shiprocket login, set a pickup address, and let orders flow across. The order you do things in matters, though, and a couple of steps are easy to skip in a way that only shows up when a real order fails to sync.

This guide covers the full connection from a fresh Shopify admin through to a tested order, and points out where Shiprocket's own help centre answers the questions that come up most often afterwards.
prerequisites: A Shopify store with at least one real product, and admin access to it
A Shiprocket account you can log into (sign up separately first; the app authorizes an existing account, it doesn't create one)
costNote: Creating a Shiprocket account costs nothing, and Shiprocket's free Lite plan covers stores shipping up to roughly 5 orders a month at standard rates. Past that volume, its paid tiers (Business at ₹199/month, Advanced at ₹499/month, Pro at ₹799/month, per Shiprocket's own pricing page) unlock better per-shipment rates and support. None of them are required just to connect the Shopify app and start shipping.

steps.heading: Get both sides ready, then start the connection
steps.body:
Two things need to exist before anything else: a Shopify store with at least one real product, and a Shiprocket account you can log into. Sign up at Shiprocket first if you haven't, since the integration authorizes an existing account instead of creating one, and the setup will stall at the login screen otherwise.

Shiprocket's own support documentation describes starting the connection from its side: in the Shiprocket dashboard, go to Setup & Manage, then Channels, click Add New Channel, and choose Shopify. From there, Connect to Shopify hands you off to a Shopify login and authorization screen. You can also reach the same app by searching Shiprocket in the Shopify App Store from your admin's Apps section; both routes end at the same authorization step, so use whichever side you happen to be in already.

image.caption: The Shopify admin home. Apps sits at the bottom of the left menu, which is one way to reach the Shiprocket app.

steps.heading: Authorize the connection with your Shiprocket login
steps.body: Signing in with your Shiprocket credentials, not creating new ones, is what links that account to this Shopify store. Use the login for the account whose wallet and courier settings you want orders billed against. If you manage more than one Shiprocket account, get this right now, since re-pointing later means disconnecting and reinstalling. Once authorized, the Shiprocket dashboard lists your Shopify store as a connected channel, and orders can start flowing across.

steps.heading: Set your pickup address and serviceable pincodes
steps.body: Shiprocket calculates rates and assigns couriers from a pickup location, so get this right before anything else works. Add the address your parcels are collected from, including the correct pincode. A wrong pincode here quietly produces wrong rates and wrong delivery estimates on every order. If you ship from more than one place, add each as a separate pickup location and mark one primary. Shiprocket's documentation notes that a single pincode can't be mapped to more than one fulfilment location, so give each pickup point its own pincode instead of reusing one. This is also where you set which pincodes you serve and whether you offer COD.

steps.heading: Configure shipping rates on the Shopify side
steps.body: Connecting Shiprocket doesn't rewrite the rates your Shopify checkout shows. In Shopify, go to Settings, then Shipping and delivery, and decide how to charge: a flat rate per order, free shipping above a threshold, or weight-based bands that roughly track what Shiprocket bills you. Whichever you pick, fill in your product weights. Shiprocket bills by weight and dimensions, so a store with no weights entered quotes customers one figure and gets charged another. Compare a few sample pincodes in Shiprocket's rate calculator against what your checkout quotes, and adjust until the gap is one you can live with.

steps.heading: Place a test order and confirm it syncs
steps.body: Buy something from your own store with a real Indian address and a low-value test product. Within a minute or two the order should appear in the Shiprocket dashboard's orders list, carrying the customer name, address, and item details from Shopify. Assign a courier and generate a label to confirm the full path works. If the order arrives but won't ship, the usual cause is a missing weight or an unserviceable pincode, not a broken connection. Check that tracking status flows back to the Shopify order too, since that's what stops customers emailing you for updates.

steps.heading: Know where to go when something breaks
steps.body: Once you're live, most problems are operational: a pincode that isn't serviceable, a product category a courier won't carry, or a login that stops working. Shiprocket runs a searchable help centre covering exactly these cases, including prohibited and dangerous goods lists and who to contact about a shipment in transit. Bookmark it before your first busy week, not during it. As a rough rule, anything about a specific shipment in transit goes to Shiprocket support, and anything about what the customer sees at checkout is a Shopify shipping setting you control.

image.caption: Shiprocket's help centre articles covering prohibited items, who to contact about a shipment, and account login problems.

troubleshooting.problem: An order placed in Shopify never shows up in Shiprocket
troubleshooting.cause: The store isn't fully authorized yet, or the order was placed before the connection finished linking.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm your Shopify store shows as a connected channel in the Shiprocket dashboard, then place a fresh test order to check.

troubleshooting.problem: Shiprocket quotes a different rate than what the customer was charged
troubleshooting.cause: Product weights weren't filled in on the Shopify side, or the Shopify shipping rate was never updated to match what Shiprocket bills.
troubleshooting.fix: Fill in accurate weights for every product, then compare a handful of sample pincodes in Shiprocket's rate calculator against your Shopify checkout and adjust the rate settings.

troubleshooting.problem: Adding a second pickup location fails or overwrites the first
troubleshooting.cause: Shiprocket won't map one pincode to more than one fulfilment location.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a genuinely different pincode for each pickup address, or consolidate shipments from that pincode under a single location.

faq.question: Do I need a Shiprocket account before installing the Shopify app?
faq.answer: Yes. The connection authorizes an account that already exists, it doesn't create one, so sign up at Shiprocket first, either from its dashboard's Channels section or from the Shopify App Store.

faq.question: Does connecting Shiprocket change the rates my customers see at checkout?
faq.answer: Not by itself. Your Shopify shipping settings still control what's quoted at checkout, so set flat, free-over-threshold, or weight-based rates there and compare them against Shiprocket's actual charges.

faq.question: Why is my Shopify order not showing in the Shiprocket dashboard?
faq.answer: Usually the store isn't fully authorized, or the order was placed before the connection completed. Check that your Shopify store is listed as a connected channel in Shiprocket, then place a fresh test order.

faq.question: Can I ship from more than one location?
faq.answer: Yes. Add each collection point as a separate pickup address in Shiprocket and mark one as primary. A single pincode can only belong to one pickup location, so use a genuinely different pincode for each.

faq.question: Who do I contact when a shipment goes missing, Shiprocket or the courier?
faq.answer: Shiprocket. Its help centre states that queries about a shipment sent through the platform go to Shiprocket support, not direct to the courier partner.

faq.question: Does using Shiprocket with Shopify cost anything?
faq.answer: Creating an account and installing the app is free, and Shiprocket's Lite plan covers up to about 5 orders a month at no monthly cost. Higher-volume stores can move to a paid tier for better per-shipment rates, but it isn't required to get connected.
